newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM to become monk, seek political calm.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM to become monk, seek political calm.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh announced on Monday that he will enter the monkhood for one week starting Thursday to ease recent political tensions.
"Sometimes politicians do not follow the religious way, so I am becoming a monk to make my own politics calm down," Ranariddh said at a school opening eastern Kampong Cham province.
He said he would shave his hair in a ceremony at the palace and then serve as a monk at a Phnom Penh temple. He said he also might travel to a monastary in India during his time as a monk.
Political tensions between Ranariddh and his coalition partner, co-Premier Hun Sen, have escalated in recent weeks.
The two leaders have been at odds over many issues including alleged incidents of political intimidation and recent gun battles between soliders loyal to each leader.

Ranariddh said that by temporarily joining the monkhood he was acting according to the traditions of the royal family, noting his father, King Norodom Sihanouk, had entered monkhood twice in the past.
He said Sihanouk had asked that he do the same.
Opposition leader Sam Rainsy entered the monkhood for several weeks last month.
